sentences.text: Goniopholis resembled living crocodilians and likely functioned as a semi-aquatic ambush predator.
Unlike modern crocodilians, this animal possessed dermal armor on its back made of two rows of large rectangular scutes with a peg and groove articulation mechanism.
The species G. kiplingi was named to honor the author Rudyard Kipling for his enthusiasm for natural sciences.
G. kiplingi had a skull reaching 475.6 mm, making it one of the largest goniopholidids.
Eggs attributed to Goniopholis have been found in the Late Jurassic of Portugal.
G. baryglyphaeus from the Late Jurassic of Portugal is the oldest known Goniopholis species.
A partial skeleton of an indeterminate Goniopholis species was recovered from the Berriasian-aged Angeac-Charente bonebed in France.
Goniopholis has been inferred to be ectothermic based on bone histology and stable isotope analysis.
The genus Goniopholis was named by Richard Owen in 1841.
Goniopholis belongs to the order Mesoeucrocodylia and the family Goniopholididae.
Goniopholis lived from the Bathonian to the Santonian, approximately 168.2 to 83.6 million years ago.
